evidence: Source review against native build 1: backend snapshots and usage responses retain their field shapes, including the UsageBackend fields decoded by UsageModels.swift. The backend update endpoint now requires owner authority; the native app has no caller of this endpoint and sends no agent actor headers. Conversation wire contracts, executor protocol, iOS build middleware, and native draft/outbox paths are unchanged. CLI selection and sealed package validation change host behavior only. Focused HTTP tests prove owner update acceptance and agent refusal before any updater runs. This review preserves the existing build floor for retained native features. No signed-device, TestFlight, reconnect, or draft-survival checks ran for this ticket. Native push review: the only additional backend change passes four explicit APNs configuration variables through the managed launcher. No HTTP payload, route, authentication contract, or minimum build changes. Release iPhone builds now enable the existing token registration path. Existing launcher integration coverage checks exact APNs configuration and rejects unsupported variables. Physical delivery proof remains pending the operator release and replacement signed build. Ticket workspace review against native build 1: the public Ticket and artifact catalog payload shapes remain unchanged. Private checkout entries are excluded, while ordinary artifact links keep the same routes and standard missing-file errors after expiry. APIClient.artifacts and ArtifactReader do not call the executor workspace registration or retirement routes. Those routes and protocol 23 concern the host executor only. Native build authentication, drafts, outbox, and minimum build policy are unchanged. Source review and existing artifact route coverage support retaining build 1. This acknowledgment is not signed-device, TestFlight, reconnect, or release-readiness evidence; no app was installed or deployed for this Ticket.
